name: Genetic Cerebral Malformation

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic variant in genes associated with cerebral malformations
MRI or CT demonstrating structural brain abnormalities consistent with cerebral malformation
Presence of neurological deficits such as developmental delay, seizures, or motor impairment

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic neuroimaging findings and genetic confirmation of pathogenic variant
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential to confirm diagnosis and differentiate from acquired malformations

pathognomonic.notes: Abnormal cortical organization with excessive small gyri
Smooth brain surface due to defective neuronal migration

common.notes: Delayed acquisition of motor and cognitive milestones
Recurrent seizures often resistant to treatment
Head circumference significantly below age norms

occasional.symptomName: Visual impairment due to optic nerve hypoplasia
occasional.notes: Reduced visual acuity related to optic nerve underdevelopment
searchTerms: poor vision from small optic nerves
optic nerve underdevelopment causing vision loss
vision problems due to optic nerve issues

occasional.notes: Accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid causing ventricular enlargement
Range from mild to severe intellectual disability

rare.notes: Facial anomalies associated with syndromic forms
Structural cardiac anomalies in syndromic cases

laboratory: Genetic testing identifying pathogenic variants in genes such as LIS1, DCX, or ARX
imaging: MRI showing cortical malformations including polymicrogyria, lissencephaly, or heterotopia
CT scan demonstrating abnormal gyral patterns and ventricular enlargement
genetic: Autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive, or X-linked inheritance patterns depending on gene involved
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) abnormalities consistent with epileptiform activity

distinguishingFeatures: History of prenatal or perinatal insult
Imaging findings consistent with acquired injury rather than developmental malformation
Presence of metabolic abnormalities on laboratory testing
Lack of characteristic cortical malformations on imaging

references: Barkovich AJ, et al. A developmental and genetic classification for malformations of cortical development. Neurology. 2012.
Dobyns WB, et al. Lissencephaly: a genetic and clinical review. Neuropediatrics. 2010.
